$meta.name: Quiet
$meta.purpose: Semantic source of truth for the Quiet family design language. Values are data, not CSS. Map them to any platform, framework or token system.
$meta.modeStrategy: Follow the operating system by default. Offer an explicit override in settings, persist per device, never per account.

$meta.rule: Use semantic roles, never raw values, in a design or a component. A role maps to the right value for the current mode.
$meta.accent: One accent for the whole family. It shifts value (not identity) between modes to keep contrast.
$meta.primaryActionIsNotAccent: Primary buttons are ink on paper in light, paper on ink in dark. The accent is never a large fill.

canvas.role: The page itself. The largest surface; warm, never pure white or pure black.

surface.role: Default raised content: cards, panels, menus, inputs when they need separation.

surfaceRaised.role: A second level for floating or nested surfaces: popovers, command palette, inspector.

surfaceSunken.role: Recessed areas: tab tracks, table headers, disabled wells, inline code.

ink.role: Primary text and icons. 16.9:1 on canvas (light), 17.3:1 (dark).

inkSecondary.role: Secondary text: descriptions, supporting values, nav labels. 5.9:1 min.

inkTertiary.role: Tertiary text: labels, timestamps, captions. 4.9:1 min on canvas — the floor, not a suggestion.

inkInverse.role: Text on ink or accent fills.

line.role: Default 1px hairline: card borders, dividers, input borders.

lineSoft.role: Quietest divider: table row separators, inner lists.

lineStrong.role: Emphasised rule: section boundaries, field borders, outlined buttons.

accent.role: The family accent. Links, active navigation indicator, primary data series, highlights.

accentHover.role: Hover/pressed state for accent text and accent-outlined elements.

accentInk.role: Text/icon on an accent-coloured fill. Rare; accent fills are discouraged.

accentWash.role: Quiet accent fill: selected nav item, selected row, app tile, inline highlight.

accentLine.role: Accent-tinted border or indicator: focus-adjacent rules, selected outlines.

focus.role: Focus ring. Always visible, 2px, 2px offset. Must meet 3:1 against the adjacent surface.

positive.role: Positive money movement, cleared, completed, healthy. Always paired with a word or symbol.

positiveWash.role: Background wash for positive status pills and inline success.

negative.role: Outflow, failure, destructive action. Always paired with a label or icon.

negativeWash.role: Background wash for error and destructive status.

warning.role: Caution, pending, attention required. Always paired with a label.

warningWash.role: Background wash for pending and attention pills.

primaryAction.role: The one filled primary control. Inverted between modes: ink in light, paper in dark.

primaryActionHover.role: Hover state for the primary action.

hover.role: Subtle hover background for ghost buttons, rows, menu items.

selected.role: Neutral selected background when the accent would be too loud (e.g. multi-select rows).

scrim.role: Modal backdrop. Never fully opaque; the page should still be legible beneath.

overlaySurface.role: Dialogs, command palette, popovers. Uses elevation 3.

skeleton.role: Loading placeholder fill. No shimmer; a slow opacity pulse at most.

disabledInk.role: Disabled label. Exempt from contrast requirements, but still legible.

appTint.$meta: Optional. Off by default. Only for the app monogram and the active-app indicator. Never for interaction, data, status or navigation.

$meta.familyRule: Exactly one sans-serif family carries the product. No serif, no display face, no decorative font in the core system.
$meta.default: System UI. On Apple platforms this is SF Pro; it is the reference rendering.
$meta.crossPlatform: If the family must look identical on Windows, Android and web, license a neutral grotesque (Söhne, Suisse Int'l, Neue Haas Grotesk) or use Inter. Do not mix it with the system stack.
$meta.trackingRule: Tighten display sizes, open labels. Never justify text. Never use all-caps for more than a short label.

ui.stack: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Text", "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif

display.stack: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Display", "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif
display.role: Page titles and hero statements. Same family as UI; optical sizing does the work.

numeric.stack: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Text", "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif
numeric.role: All money, counts, dates in tables and KPI values.

mono.stack: ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, "Roboto Mono", Consolas, monospace
mono.role: Code, identifiers, hashes, technical strings. Never for general UI numbers.

interFallback.adjustment: Use Inter only when cross-platform consistency is required. Add +0.01em to body tracking to compensate for its wider defaults.

display-1.use: First-run, marketing, an empty state with a point of view.

display-2.use: The page title in an application. One per screen.

title-1.use: Object detail title, dialog title on large screens.

heading.use: Card titles, small groups, form section titles.

body-sm.use: Secondary descriptions, table cells, helper text.

label.use: Eyebrows, field labels, KPI labels, column headers.

micro.use: Status pills, footnotes, metadata at the edge of legibility.

rules: Do not invent sizes between the scale steps. If a screen needs a new size, the screen is over-designed.
Use attention (bold/ink) selectively. The default reading colour is inkSecondary when the text is supporting, ink when it is the content.
Body copy measures 45–70 characters. Use `max-width: 62ch` for prose.
Numerals in columns, KPI values and chart labels are always tabular and lining.
Labels are uppercase with 0.14em tracking. Never uppercase a sentence.

$meta.rule: Use only the steps below. Prefer a smaller number of larger gaps over many small ones. Space is the primary separator.

density.$meta: Comfortable is the default. Compact is for data-heavy surfaces, not for the whole product. Never mix densities within one form.

usage.lg: dialogs, drawers, command palette, large overlays

border.rule: A 1px line is the default boundary. Use a 2px rule only for a section opening or a focus ring.

elevation.$meta: Quiet uses light to separate layers, not to decorate. Cards are e0. Only transient surfaces are elevated.

rules: Popovers, drawers, dialogs: base, enter on open, exit on close.
No bounce, no spring, no looping animation in the core system.
Under prefers-reduced-motion, remove non-essential duration; keep opacity changes at instant.

icon.rule: Line icons only. No filled icons except status dots and the app monogram. Icons are 16px in navigation and controls, 20px in page headers.

behaviour.md: Rail collapses to monograms only; sidebar can become a sheet on demand.
behaviour.sm: Sidebar becomes a sheet; single column; tables scroll or cardify.
behaviour.xs: Single column; page actions move to a sticky bottom bar when consequential.

dataViz.$meta: Muted, distinguishable, and never dependent on hue alone. Use direct labels where possible; a legend is a last resort.
rules: Axis labels are 9.5px uppercase with 0.07em tracking.
Lines are 1.8px; the primary series is 2px. No area fill above 12% opacity.
Never use more than four series in one chart. If you need more, the chart is a table.
Direct-label the final point or the largest value; do not rely on a legend for a single series.

button.rule: One primary (filled) button per view or dialog. Secondary is outlined. Tertiary is ghost. Destructive is outlined in negative, filled only inside a confirm dialog.

input.rule: Labels sit above fields. Helper text below. Errors replace helper text and use negative with an icon.

table.rule: Row separators only; no vertical grid lines. Numeric columns right-aligned and tabular. Status is the last column unless it is the primary filter.

avatar.rule: Initials only for people; monograms for apps. No photographic avatars in the core system.

focusRing.rule: Visible on every interactive element, including custom controls. Use the same ring in light and dark.

$meta.verified: All text roles below are verified against their intended surface in both modes.
